proof_summary: For \(k\ge 60\), set \(n=2k+1\); a nonzero determinant forces some matrix entry to be \(1\), yielding primes \(n+i-j\) and \(n+j-i\), whose symmetric offsets cancel so their sum is \(2n=4k+2\). The remaining cases \(1\le k<60\) are handled by an explicit finite list of prime decompositions.
